summary:
Every rating across the board is scorching the same four categories right now, and that uniformity is the headline. R1 through R4 are all sitting at 8-2 (80%) over the last 14 days in trends, runs, and hitting, with sp also running hot at 80% and riding identical 3-game win streaks. That's not noise — it's four independently-weighted models converging on the same signal, which is exactly when RJ should lean hardest. The one glaring exception is bullpen_fatigue, which is ice cold across all four ratings: 4-6 (40%) over 14 days with a 5-game losing streak on every single rating. Fade anything where bullpen_fatigue is the deciding category today, full stop — it's underwater against a 45-47% season baseline and actively bleeding.

On today's board, prioritize games where trends+sp or trends+runs agree — those combos hit 58.0% (370-268, n=638) and 57.3% (404-301, n=705) for the season and are the strongest category pairings in the model. R2 is the rating to trust most if there's a strong-play game on tap: it's 6-1 (86%, +5.0u) over the last 14 days and 11-4 (73%, +9.0u) over 30, the best recent unit return of the group. R1 and R3 are close behind at 4-1 (80%, +2.0u) in the same window, so any slate where all three ratings stack a strong play together is a green light. If MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD show up as model picks today, lean in without hesitation — MIL is 51-23 (69%) on picks and 29-13 (+18.0u) on strong plays, TBR is 44-19 (70%, +21.0u strong), and LAD's strong-play number is the best in the sample at 28-7 (80%, +27.0u). Conversely, if NYY pops up as a pick, treat it skeptically — 49% straight-up and -4.0u on strong plays makes it the one team-level red flag worth overriding a hot rating for.
